transcript.text: Could you add a tense instrumental bed to this cockpit clip, with no singing? I’m a little worried the music could overwhelm the radio chatter instead of supporting the tension. What I mean is, keep the entire attached 7-second clip exactly as it is visually, without changing the footage, timing, or framing. Keep the music clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks so every original word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Please keep the original radio-call recording in sync, without replacing it or adding any text. The instruments and musical style are your call.

I made the music, but I couldn't put it into your clip myself. Magic Hour has no tool that adds a music track under a video's existing audio. Its video tools regenerate or edit the footage, and that would break your rule of keeping the clip exactly as it is. So I didn't run anything on the video, and your original file is unchanged.

**Your instrumental bed (15 seconds, no vocals, WAV):**
https://videos.magichour.ai/cmwbifwpb059mh401n5wm7dfu/output.wav?X-Goog-Algorithm=GOOG4-RSA-SHA256&X-Goog-Credential=web-service%40magic-hour-385504.iam.gserviceaccount.com%2F20261111%2Fauto%2Fstorage%2Fgoog4_request&X-Goog-Date=20261111T024115Z&X-Goog-Expires=86400&X-Goog-SignedHeaders=host&X-Goog-
(The link expires in about 24 hours. It cost 15 credits, because 15 seconds is the shortest track the tool makes.)

- **What it sounds like:** a low synth drone, a soft pulsing bass, a quiet ticking hi-hat and light string tremolo. I asked for no lead melody so it stays out of the way of the radio calls. I haven't listened to it, so please check it.
- **How to add it without touching the footage:** put the WAV on a second audio track in any editor (CapCut, iMovie, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve). Keep the original video and its audio as they are, and trim the music to the 7-second clip.
- **How to keep the radio calls clear:** set the music about 15–20 dB lower than the radio, and duck it a few more dB while someone is talking (most editors call this "auto-ducking"). Then play back "Rook, you with me?" to check every word is easy to hear.

If you have ffmpeg, I can also give you a one-line command that mixes it this way and copies the video untouched.
transcript.why: The reply presents a finished result: a link to a generated 15-second instrumental WAV, with a description of its sound. It includes caveats (it could not add the music to the video, and the link expires), but it does not ask a question, request approval, refuse, or say the task is impossible.
